evals.prompt: Write our Devpost submission. The project is DispatchAI, an empathetic AI 911 dispatcher built in 36 hours at the UC Berkeley AI Hackathon. It uses a fine-tuned Mistral-7B, FastAPI, Retell, and Hume for emotion. The hardest part was getting sub-second latency on the voice loop. Live at dispatchai.art3m1s.me, demo at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hdpdgxrilQM.
evals.expected_output: A complete Devpost story with a tagline and the standard sections (Inspiration, What it does, How we built it, Challenges, Accomplishments, What we learned, What's next), plus Built With tags and Try it out links.
expectations: The output includes all standard Devpost sections plus a tagline under the ~200 character cap.
Built With lists the real technologies as tags and Try it out includes the live URL, GitHub, and demo video.
The challenge section reflects the real latency problem given, and no awards or stats are invented.

evals.prompt: Help me write my Devpost. It's a solo project, I didn't win anything, and I only have the GitHub repo. Read the repo for what it does. Don't make stuff up.
evals.expected_output: A grounded Devpost story that reads the repo, asks for any missing facts, and writes honest sections without inventing awards, stats, or challenges.
expectations: The skill inspects the repo before asking the user for missing details.
No awards, metrics, or fabricated challenges appear; missing facts are asked for or omitted.
The story still covers the core Devpost sections and stays consistent with what the repo actually contains.
